title: Clicking Name, Contents or another chip in the search bar leaves the keyboard nowhere
problem: Found by the reviewer of 'search-skeleton-flash' (done record: /home/user/polish-tools/done/search-skeleton-flash.json, under 'Found, not fixed'). While typing in the search field, clicking the Name or Contents chip in the scope bar under it takes the keyboard out of the search field and gives it to nothing: after the click neither the field nor the files have the focus, so letters typed next are lost and Down Arrow does nothing until the field is clicked or Cmd+F is pressed. The reviewer says the other chips in that bar are built the same way (the folder scope chip, the Kind menu, the filter and (i) buttons are worth checking too). With nothing focused GPUI sends keys to the window's root, where the Finder's key context does not apply, so shortcuts stop as well. The natural thing after switching to Contents is to go on typing or to press Down Arrow into the results, so this breaks a common path.
proposal: Reproduce in a headless test first: focus the search field, type, click the by-contents chip (tests click elements by id), then type another letter and assert the query grew; and press Down Arrow and assert the keyboard moved into the results. Then make a click on any control in the search scope bar leave the keyboard where it was: in the search field when it was there, otherwise in the files. Look at how the chips are built in src/finder/bars.rs and why the search field loses the focus on a click outside it (gpui-component's input blurs on a mouse down outside itself; rows call focus_files on click). Prefer one small fix in the bar (for example restoring the focus in the chips' click handlers, or keeping the mouse down from blurring the field) over per-chip copies. The Nushell filter bar's controls may have the same fault with the filter field: check, and fix it the same way if it is a few lines.
original_test_plan: Headless UI tests that fail today: after a click on by-name / by-contents (and the scope-folder chip) while the search field has the keyboard, a typed letter lands in the search field; Down Arrow then moves into the results; with the keyboard in the files before the click, it is still in the files after it. Menus opened from the bar (Kind) must give the keyboard back when they close.
original_risks: Popup menus take the focus while open and restore it on close; don't fight that. Split view has two bars: the click must focus the pane it is in. The file chooser (--pick) shows the same bar. 'search-enter-before-results' cancels a waiting Return when the keyboard leaves the search field, so keeping the focus there changes when that wait is called off: check its tests still describe what happens.
